```{.quiz-yaml}
id: 18_regression_flat_line
title: What if the population line were flat?
questions:
  - id: sample_slope
    type: multiple-choice
    prompt: >
      Suppose coffee had nothing to do with test scores in the population, so
      the population slope is exactly zero. We take a sample of seven students
      and fit the least-squares line. What should we expect of the sample slope?
    options:
      - text: Exactly zero in every sample
      - text: It would vary from sample to sample and usually be nonzero
        correct: true
      - text: Negative in every sample
    explanation: >
      Just as a sample mean usually misses the population mean, the sample
      slope will usually miss zero. The line tilts to follow whatever ups
      and downs happen to be in the sample.

  - id: sample_ss_regression
    type: multiple-choice
    prompt: >
      If the fitted line tilts, what does that tell us about $SS_{regression}$?
    options:
      - text: Exactly zero
      - text: Above zero
        correct: true
      - text: Below zero
    explanation: >
      Above zero. If the best-fit line tilts, it saves some squared error
      compared with guessing the mean. That can happen by chance, even when
      the population slope is zero.
```
